messages:
anya: Heads-up — noticed p95 on the service breakdown chart is consistently higher than the endpoint p95s when combined into the composite. Screenshot incoming.

maria: can you drop the screenshot and the endpoint IDs?

anya: https://.../screenshot.png here. It looks like the composite line is using different sampling bucket than each endpoint panel. @eng-platform any idea? :thinking_face:

aj: likely sampling mismatch. composite uses the rollup pre-aggregation which samples at 1%, while per-endpoint panels use raw samples from the router (100% for short traces).

leo: that sounds like the tdigest rollup vs native histogram thing. Rollups compress distribution and can bias pctl on multi-modal latencies.

anya: hmm, but the composite p95 > endpoints p95 by ~40ms. If rollup underestimates tails I'd expect lower composites, not higher.

aj: good point. It can go either way depending on which buckets get trimmed. Also note we do route-weighting before merge; if one noisy endpoint has higher weight in the composite it could pull the p95 up.

leo: here's a quick query snippet I ran in console: 
```
SELECT tdigest_percentile(0.95, tdigest) AS p95 FROM rollups WHERE service = 'inference' GROUP BY window(1m)
```
vs
```
SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) AS p95 FROM raw_spans WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' GROUP BY window(1m)
```

maria: OK that helps. So we have two axes of difference: sample source (rollup vs raw) and aggregation unit (service-composite vs per-endpoint then median-of-endpoints). Need to be explicit in UI.

anya: agreed. Users keep assuming p95 is comparable across panels. We should add an annotation/legend row that states "sample source: rollup/raw" and a tooltip explaining the aggregation path.

console-bot: auto-note: created ticket INF-4521 "Dashboard: make percentile sample source explicit" assigned to eng-platform.

sahil: quick UX suggestion — add a small pill next to p50/p95/p99 that toggles between "composite(rollup)" and "decomposed(raw)" and also expose the sample count per time bucket. 

leo: exposing sample_count per bucket is key. Right now composite hides effective sample weight. If we show counts users can see when pctl is unreliable.

aj: from infra side we can surface a small per-panel metric: "effective_sample_rate" and a link to the merge policy. Implementation note: computing exact sample_count for rollups requires storing counts in rollup proto (we have it but not surfaced).

maria: sounds good. proposal: (1) add legend pill + tooltip; (2) surface sample_count under the sparkline; (3) add alert rule when composite p95 deviates > 30% vs weighted per-endpoint p95 and effective_sample_rate < 5%.

anya: +1. also add a short blurb in docs/observability about "when percentiles disagree" and how to interpret rollups vs raw.

aj: I'll scope the ETA. infra work to surface counts + small API change ~2d. UI + docs ~3d. Can we ship a minimal tooltip first?

maria: tooltip first is low-risk. if you can add the API field "sample_source" returning "rollup|raw|mixed" we can wire the pill disabled state when mixed.

aj: noted. will add API field.

sahil: for the alerting rule wording please avoid fragile thresholds — maybe use a ratio + minimum sample count. Example: if composite_p95 / weighted_endpoints_p95 > 1.3 AND sample_count < 1000 then fire.

leo: last thought: run a quick audit of historical dashboards — we might have churned important incidents because people misread composite percentiles. I can help grep for alerts that had p95-based runbooks.

anya: thanks everyone. I'll summarize and add to INF-4521 and ping support to update any KBs. :thumbsup:
